In the morning at El Tatio, white steam rises above the dry high-altitude landscape. Fumaroles and pools of hot water reveal the area's geothermal activity.

Trips here start early to see the geothermal field in the cold morning air. On the return journey, visitors stop in high-altitude valleys and the small settlement of Machuca.

El Tigre lies in the mountains beyond Santa Elena in the Monteverde area. Here, a forest river forms four waterfalls. Trails wind through humid forest, follow the water and cross small bridges; this is a destination for an active walk over uneven terrain.

Descending and climbing sections, wet rocks and river crossings make the route considerably more demanding than an ordinary walk in a park. Views of the surrounding mountains depend on cloud cover. Some visit options include horseback riding during the final part of the route. The services included depend on the selected excursion.

## Volcanic Caldera and Golden Frogs: What to See in El Valle, Panama

### El Valle, Panama's Green Town!

Officially known as El Valle de Antón, this picturesque town sits within the crater of an extinct volcano, surrounded by lush forests and high mountains.

## El Valle for Nature Lovers!

El Valle is a popular weekend getaway for city residents. It is an ideal destination for walking, hiking and horseback riding, thanks to the extensive network of trails leading from town into the mountains and around the valley. Nature and bird enthusiasts come not only to walk but also to observe wildlife in its natural habitat. El Valle has several small but beautiful waterfalls. Its main attraction, however, is the rare golden frog, found only here.

The Emberá community is reached by traditional canoe through tropical forest. On the riverbank, visitors begin to learn about local residents, their traditions and their close relationship with nature.

During the visit, hosts explain medicinal plants, show handmade crafts and introduce their music and dances. The program also includes traditional cuisine and lunch before the journey continues to Gamboa. The Word itinerary does not name a specific community: this stop is confirmed at booking while preserving the trip's cultural program.
